documents.title: Mrs. May and the green girl
From the earth to the stars

stories.title: The twelve months
stories.setting: A snowy landscape and Anna's home, during January and the changing months.
stories.theme: Kindness is rewarded, while greed can lead people astray.
mainEvents: Anna's stepmother sends her into the January snow to find flowers for the stepsister.
Anna meets the twelve months, who move time forward from January through February to spring in March.
Flowers bloom, and Anna returns with a full basket and tells what happened.
The stepmother and stepsister seek the months for gifts, become lost, and Anna lives happily on her own.

stories.title: The dragon
stories.setting: A town beneath remote southern mountains, a temple, and the dragon's castle.
stories.theme: Courage joined with wise preparation can defeat a powerful threat.
mainEvents: A dragon demands food from a town and turns a man to stone with its fiery breath.
A boy asks a temple sage for help and follows directions to collect a meteor.
The sage forges a sword and tells the boy to cover himself with foul-smelling weeds.
The boy sneaks into the castle, kills the sleeping dragon, and brings its treasure home.

stories.title: The battle of Thermopylae
stories.setting: The narrow mountain pass at Thermopylae in ancient Greece.
stories.theme: Steadfast courage can endure even when victory is unlikely.
mainEvents: A Spartan leader prepares 300 men to hold a narrow entrance against a huge Persian force.
Persian arrows are stopped by shields, and the Spartans roll logs onto attackers.
The small force fights for three days with little sleep.
The Persians find a way through and kill the Spartan chief and his men; the battle remains famous.

stories.title: The deer and his image
stories.setting: A rocky forest with thick trees and shaded places.
stories.theme: Useful strengths matter more than attractive appearance.
mainEvents: The deer admires his chest and horns but dislikes his thin legs and hooves.
A dog wakes and chases him through the forest.
The deer's legs and hard hooves carry him over rocks, while his horns catch in branches and his chest cannot pass between trees.
He escapes and learns to value the features that truly helped him.

stories.title: May 29,1953
stories.setting: The summit of Mount Everest on May 29, 1953.
stories.theme: A difficult achievement is shared, remembered, and celebrated.
mainEvents: The expedition reaches the summit of Mount Everest on May 29, 1953.
The narrator observes the snow-covered, silent landscape and photographs it as proof.
The team turns back after a short time at the summit.
John Hunt congratulates the climbers, and the narrator sends word to relatives that the team is safe.

stories.title: The frog prince
stories.setting: A pool and the royal palace in a kingdom abroad.
stories.theme: Promises carry responsibility, even when keeping them is inconvenient.
mainEvents: The princess drops her bear sculpture into a pool, and a frog offers to retrieve it for a promise.
She promises that he may share her bed but runs away after he returns the sculpture.
The king insists that she keep her word, and she kisses the frog in the morning.
The frog becomes a prince who explains witches cursed him, but he refuses marriage because she broke her promise.

stories.title: A beautiful bird
stories.setting: A researcher's home, an overseas colony, a volcano, and ancient ruins.
stories.theme: Persistence can turn an unproven idea into a discovery.
mainEvents: A sailor tells biologist Dr. Norton about a talking bird, but his colleagues doubt it.
Dr. Norton travels to the colony and Jai guides him toward a volcano.
After searching for weeks without success, Dr. Norton turns back.
He hears a greeting at old ruins, discovers the bird, cages it, and returns home.

stories.title: Tricky turtle
stories.setting: A race path from a riverbank through a valley to a hill.
stories.theme: Careful teamwork can outwit speed and overconfidence.
mainEvents: Ricky boasts no one can beat him, and Tera challenges him to race to a hill.
Tera admits to her family that she plans to cheat and gives them instructions.
Her relatives wear matching white feathers and take positions along the route.
Ricky sees a turtle ahead at each point, exhausts himself, and reaches the hill after Tera's sister.

stories.title: The tale of bartelby O’Boyle
stories.setting: A divided kingdom in disorder and its capital city.
stories.theme: Cooperation and generosity can bring aid to people in need.
mainEvents: Bartelby is forced to work for the royal family and resents the unfair life.
A struggle for authority divides the kingdom, and he escapes during the disorder.
He decides to help hungry people and defends Gilliam from attackers in the capital.
Bartelby and Gilliam take surplus food from the rich and give it to the poor, earning admiration.

stories.title: Blackbeard
stories.setting: A pirate ship in fog, a coastal town, and a fishing boat at sea.
stories.theme: Past actions can continue to shape a person's future.
mainEvents: A narrator sees Blackbeard aboard a pirate ship in thick fog.
Blackbeard attacks ships, takes townspeople, and demands medicine for sick pirates.
A reward and the prospect of trial lead him to quit piracy and become a fisherman.
The Royal Navy finds him at sea, kills him, and leaves his story to be retold.

stories.title: Dinosaur drawings
stories.setting: Carl's rainy morning, school, and an imagined dinosaur exhibition.
stories.theme: Imagination is exciting, but responsibilities still need attention.
mainEvents: Carl wakes late with unfinished homework and is sent to school in rain.
His teacher sends him to the principal over his umbrella, and he struggles with a geography test.
He draws a dinosaur and imagines it becoming famous and exhibited at school.
The teacher calls time, and Carl realizes he has not finished the real test.

stories.title: The mean chef
stories.setting: A poorly managed restaurant.
stories.theme: Leaders must accept responsibility for the way they treat others.
mainEvents: The chef overcharges customers, fails to repair the oven, and mistreats workers.
Cooks oppose him and tie him up so they can run the restaurant.
They lower prices, cook with good ingredients, and make the restaurant welcoming.
The chef recognizes that he caused the problems and offers customers a free meal.

stories.title: The cat and the fox
stories.setting: A mountain peak and nearby forest where wolves approach.
stories.theme: One reliable plan is better than many confused ideas.
mainEvents: The fox boasts that he has countless escape plans, while the cat has only one.
The fox offers to teach the cat, who says her plan always works.
Wolves appear, and the cat immediately climbs a tree.
The fox hesitates over which plan to use and is caught by the wolves.

stories.title: The good student
stories.setting: Sue's dormitory, a physics test, and the school nurse's office.
stories.theme: Rest is part of learning and caring for oneself.
mainEvents: Sue prepares carefully for school but has slept very little while completing work and studying.
During a physics test, her vision blurs and she briefly cannot see clearly.
She insists on finishing a portion of the test before going to the nurse.
The nurse warns that overwork can have severe effects, and Sue begins getting enough rest.

stories.title: The lucky knife
stories.setting: A muddy archaeological dig site and the crew's tent.
stories.theme: A discovery may inspire further success, and shared finds can benefit the public.
mainEvents: A narrator joins an uncle and a contracted student crew searching for historical objects for a school foundation.
After weeks without a find, the narrator digs through wet soil and mud.
The narrator uncovers an old knife whose inscription promises good luck and keeps it in a tent.
The next day the crew finds pots, jewelry, and weapons, which the uncle donates to a committee.

stories.title: Prince Sam
stories.setting: A palace kitchen and the prince's chamber.
stories.theme: Experiencing another person's responsibilities can change one's perspective.
mainEvents: Sam accompanies his mother, a palace cook, but wanders away from the kitchen.
He meets Prince Bertram, who looks just like him, and agrees to exchange places for a week.
Sam finds royal life full of documents and a cold chamber, while Bertram struggles without servants.
They resume their own lives and appreciate them more.

stories.title: Henry ford’s famous car
stories.setting: Detroit and the Ford Motor Company in the early 1900s.
stories.theme: Practical innovation can make useful technology available to more people.
mainEvents: Henry Ford becomes a mechanic despite his father's wish that he run the family farm.
He starts Ford Motor Company in 1903 and continues after its early struggles.
He introduces the Model T in 1908 with interchangeable parts that speed assembly.
Over 19 years he sells more than 15 million cars, showing that people will buy affordable vehicles.

stories.title: The priest
stories.setting: A monastery and the priest's home and garden.
stories.theme: Joy can grow when people make time for activities they love.
mainEvents: A capable young priest feels unhappy and asks a group of monks for advice.
The monks tell him to investigate the parts of his life he loves.
He draws cartoons, keeps a diary, plants grain, makes berry jam, and paints his ceiling.
He realizes happiness is easier to find when he does things he enjoys.

stories.title: Mrs. May and the green girl
stories.setting: A small town, a stream, and a home near the woods.
stories.theme: Kindness and patience help people welcome someone unfamiliar.
mainEvents: Townspeople find a frightened green-skinned girl by a stream and suspect her intentions.
Mrs. May asks them not to reject the girl and adopts her despite the judge's doubts.
The girl communicates with drawings and explains that her people live in tree nests and eat leaves.
Mrs. May gives her home-cooked food, her skin loses its green color, and the town welcomes her.

stories.title: Albert Einstein
stories.setting: Germany, Italy, Switzerland, and Einstein's scientific career.
stories.theme: Persistence through hardship can lead to recognition and meaningful work.
mainEvents: Einstein is interested in mathematics and statistics from elementary school.
His family loses its income and moves from Germany to Italy; he later studies in Switzerland.
Other scientists initially reject his work, but recognition grows over time.
He explains the size of stars and motion of atoms, invents a refrigerator, and keeps working.

stories.title: From the earth to the stars
stories.setting: An underground mine, an open field, and a space mission.
stories.theme: A frightening turning point can give someone courage to pursue a long-held dream.
mainEvents: Jeremy works as a miner but spends nights gazing at stars through a telescope.
A flood traps him underground, where he hears an angel tell him not to return to mining.
Other miners rescue him, and he studies for two years to become an astronaut.
He joins a space mission, sees satellites and an angel, and thanks it.

stories.title: The farm festival
stories.setting: A farmyard between a barn and the farmer's garage.
stories.theme: Shared fun and helping one another can matter more than winning.
mainEvents: Farm animals plan a race whose winner would receive apples.
They repair an unstable cart, and a puppy knocks the apples over.
A duck tries to steal apples, then a fire in the barn interrupts the race again.
A journalist records the animals' views; the pig says that having fun mattered most.

stories.title: The clever thief
stories.setting: A royal tomb built with a marked stone in its roof.
stories.theme: A generous motive does not erase the consequences of stealing.
mainEvents: A king builds a tomb to keep his gold after death.
The builder marks a light roof stone and secretly enters the tomb night after night to take gold for the poor.
The king notices the shortage and hides a guard, who wounds the builder.
The guard follows blood drops and captures the builder, who says he gave away all the gold.

stories.title: The doctor’s cure
stories.setting: A hospital room and James's home after his injury.
stories.theme: Work should leave room for relationships and everyday joys.
mainEvents: Busy doctor James rarely sees his son Steve.
James slips on liquid and falls on broken glass, injuring himself.
Steve visits, shares a movie and reading, and James notices small pleasures again.
James regrets not spending enough time with Steve and chooses to go home and rest.

stories.title: The criminal
stories.setting: A jail, a forest, and a neat cabin behind a fence.
stories.theme: Understanding and compassion can encourage someone to change.
mainEvents: A thief escapes jail and finds food in a cabin in the woods.
The elderly owner catches him, sees through his lie that he is a policeman, and identifies him as a criminal.
The thief admits what he did and offers cash to settle the matter.
The owner refuses money, forgives him without a penalty, and inspires him never to steal again.

stories.title: The two captains
stories.setting: Two cotton-carrying ships approaching a hurricane and coral reef.
stories.theme: Good leaders know when safety must come before entertainment.
mainEvents: Thomas leads a strict but reliable ship, while William runs a grand ship with a carefree crew.
Thomas spots a hurricane and warns William about the reef and coral ahead.
William tells his crew to go below deck and keep dancing instead of turning back.
His ship is driven into the reef, floods, and is lost; the crew blames his poor leadership.

stories.title: The Duke and the Minister
stories.setting: The duke's tobacco fields and jail.
stories.theme: Careful investigation can expose false accusations.
mainEvents: The duke's tobacco plants begin dying, and guards blame a woman for singing unfamiliar words.
The woman says she is ordinary, while the minister believes she is innocent.
The minister examines a plant and finds small bugs eating it.
He uses his resemblance to the duke to free her and apologizes; the duke stays focused on the plants.

stories.title: The fisherman
stories.setting: A bridge by the water near an inn.
stories.theme: Patience and confidence can matter more than elaborate equipment.
mainEvents: A fisherman catches fish with a branch, line, hook, and net.
George challenges him and brings electronic tools to locate and weigh fish.
They fish all day, and George subtracts his catch from the fisherman's total.
The fisherman has 47 more fish and explains that patience and self-belief are his method.

stories.title: Osiris and the Nile
stories.setting: Ancient Egypt along the fertile Nile River.
stories.theme: Love and care for a community can outlast betrayal.
mainEvents: Osiris and Isis teach the Egyptians useful skills and receive a pyramid as a gift.
Set envies Osiris and traps him in a wooden box during an annual tour.
The box is carried by a flood to a foreign shore, where Isis recovers Osiris's body and obtains a grave.
The gods honor Isis's love, make Osiris god of the underworld, and he returns every spring to help crops.

stories.title: The taxi driver
stories.setting: Peter's taxi downtown and the Fourth Street Bank.
stories.theme: Honesty and kindness can open an unexpected opportunity.
mainEvents: Taxi driver Peter hopes to study with a scholarship and work at a bank.
A rude passenger asks to be driven to Fourth Street Bank and cannot find his wallet.
Peter lends him the exact fare despite being upset by the passenger's behavior.
The passenger reveals he founded the bank, offers money, and hires Peter because he is honest.
